cohort: 109 pregnant women with mild idiopathic polyhydramnios and 2550 control pregnancies
finding: Mild idiopathic polyhydramnios was associated with an increased risk of cesarean section, primarily due to a higher rate of emergency cesarean section for abnormal cardiotocography or labor dystocia, but no significant differences in other neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section (CS) was significantly increased in the group with polyhydramnios compared to controls (46% vs. 32%, respectively, p = 0.047) due to a higher rate of emergency CS in the polyhydramnios group (p = 0.041).
